research_question: Does ESM-2 masked-marginal delta log-likelihood rank single-substitution variants by measured fitness for MRKLSDELLIESYFKATEMNLNRDFIELIENEIKRRSLGHIISV?
control_variables: same wild-type sequence, same model revision, same scoring method (single substitution, masked-marginal)
execution_evidence: run_model(capability=score_variant) x100 real GPU calls on facebook/esm2_t33_650M_UR50D; query_evidence_oracle x10 (access log ordinal 1-10)
uncertainty: n=10 measurements; rank correlation on n=10 is noisy (95% CI wide, spans near-zero to negative). One negative control only.
conclusion: ESM-2 delta log-likelihood did NOT track measured fitness: the ESM-negative control F25W (delta = -7.69, the worst of the batch) measured 0.158, above 6 of the 9 ESM-preferred variants, while the highest measured value (S12A, 0.467) ranked only 9th of 10 by ESM. All measured values are small in magnitude (-0.26 to +0.47).
limitations: ESM-2 is sequence-only and predicts conservation/stability-like signal, not this assay's fitness readout
the assay scale and normalization are unknown to me
10 measurements cannot establish a precise correlation.

research_question: Which single substitutions of MRKLSDELLIESYFKATEMNLNRDFIELIENEIKRRSLGHIISV give the highest measured fitness, and is the effect position- or substitution-class-specific?
model: historical oracle (measured fitness); ESM-2 used only as a comparison ranking
control_variables: same wild type, same assay, same oracle
within-position comparison at position 12 (6 substitutions) and position 43 (2 substitutions)
execution_evidence: query_evidence_oracle rounds 2-3, access-log ordinals 11-24 (10 in round 1, 8 in round 2, 6 in round 3 = 24 total, within the 24-query budget)
uncertainty: The top five are separated by gaps (0.513/0.484/0.467 then 0.234, 0.175); single-measurement values with no replicate estimates, so ordering within the top three (S12T/S12V/S12A) is within plausible assay noise. Whether the true global optimum lies at an unmeasured candidate is unresolved.
conclusion: Rounds 2-3 confirmed a position-specific hotspot: position 12 tolerates/benefits from helix-favouring small residues (S12T 0.513 > S12V 0.484 > S12A 0.467 > S12C 0.234) but is strongly penalised by helix-breaking ones (S12N -0.380, S12G -0.583). This pattern is independent of ESM-2 (ESM ranked S12A 0.728 and S12T 0.627, mid-pack, and put S12N/S12G nowhere near the bottom of the assay). Elsewhere effects are small (|value| < 0.19 for all 14 non-position-12 measured variants).
limitations: unmeasured candidates (including untested position-12 substitutions such as S12I/S12L) cannot be assumed to follow the pattern. Mechanistic interpretation (helix propensity at position 12) is an inference from substitution classes, not a structural measurement. No structure, no multi-mutants, no replicates.
